column1: Ancient voyagers who settled the far-flung islands of the Pacific Ocean
column2: 那些在太平洋遥远岛屿上定居的古代航海者

column1: An important archaeological discovery on the island of Efate in the Pacific archipelago of Vanuatu has revealed traces of an ancient seafaring people, the distant ancestors of today’s Polynesians.
column2: 在太平洋瓦努阿图群岛的埃法特岛上，一项重要的考古发现揭示了一个古代航海民族的踪迹。他们是今天波利尼西亚人的远祖。

column1: The site came to light only by chance.
column2: 这个地点是偶然被发现的。

column1: An agricultural worker, digging in the grounds of a derelict plantation, scraped open a grave—the first of dozens in a burial ground some 3,000 years old.
column2: 一名农业工人在一处废弃种植园的场地里挖掘时，无意中刮开了第一座坟墓——这是数千年前一个墓地中的数十座坟墓中的第一座。

column1: It is the oldest cemetery ever found in the Pacific islands, and it harbors the remains of an ancient people archaeologists call the Lapita.
column2: 这是太平洋岛屿上发现的最古老的墓地，里面埋藏着一些古代人的遗骸，考古学家将这群人称为拉皮塔人。

column1: They were daring blue-water adventurers who used basic canoes to rove across the ocean.
column2: 他们是勇敢的远洋探险家，使用简单的独木舟在海洋上航行。

column1: But they were not just explorers.
column2: 但他们不仅仅是探险家。

column1: They were also pioneers who carried with them everything they would need to build new lives—their livestock, taro seedlings and stone tools.
column2: 他们也是先驱者，带着一切必要的物资来建设新的生活家园——他们的牲畜、芋苗，以及石器工具。

column1: Within the span of several centuries, the Lapita stretched the boundaries of their world from the jungle-clad volcanoes of Papua New Guinea to the loneliest coral outliers of Tonga.
column2: 在几个世纪的时间里，拉皮塔人将他们的疆域扩展到了从巴布亚新几内亚那些被丛林覆盖的火山地带，一直到汤加最偏远的海岛。

column1: The Lapita left precious few clues about themselves, but Efate expands the volume of data available to researchers dramatically.
column2: 拉皮塔人留下的有关自身的线索少之又少，但埃法特岛的发现大大增加了研究者可用的资料。

column1: The remains of 62 individuals have been uncovered so far, and archaeologists were also thrilled to find six complete Lapita pots.
column2: 到目前为止，已经发现了62个人的遗骸，考古学家们还非常兴奋地发现了六个完整的拉皮塔陶器。

column1: Other items included a Lapita burial urn with modeled birds arranged on the rim as though peering down at the human remains sealed inside.
column2: 其他出土物还包括一件拉皮塔葬瓮，瓮口边缘排列着塑成鸟形的装饰，看起来仿佛正低头细看封存在瓮里的遗骸。

column1: ‘It’s an important discovery’, says Matthew Spriggs, professor of archaeology at the Australian National University and head of the international team digging up the site, ‘for it conclusively identifies the remains as Lapita.’
column2: “这是一项重要的发现，”马修·斯普里格斯说。他是澳大利亚国立大学考古学教授，也是发掘这一遗址的国际团队负责人。“因为这确凿地表明，这些遗骸属于拉皮塔人。”
column4: professor of archaeology|n. 考古学教授

column1: DNA teased from these human remains may help answer one of the most puzzling questions in Pacific anthropology: did all Pacific islanders spring from one source or many?
column2: 从这些人类遗骸中提取的DNA可能有助于解答太平洋地区人类学中最令人困惑的问题之一：所有的太平洋岛民都是来自同一个源头，还是由多个群体演化而来？

column1: Was there only one outward migration from a single point in Asia, or several from different points?
column2: 是从亚洲的一个地方出发的，还是从多个不同的地方出发的？

column1: ‘This represents the best opportunity we’ve had yet,’ says Spriggs, ‘to find out who the Lapita actually were, where they came from, and who their closest descendants are today.’
column2: “这确实是我们迄今为止所遇到的最佳机会，”斯普里格斯说，“我们可以借此了解拉皮塔人究竟是谁，他们来自哪里，以及他们的后代今天是谁。”

column1: There is one stubborn question for which archaeology has yet to provide any answers: how did the Lapita accomplish the ancient equivalent of a moon landing, many times over?
column2: 有一道难题，考古学至今还没能给出答案：拉皮塔人如何一次又一次完成了在古代堪比登月的壮举？
column3: stubborn question|n. 久未解决的难题
column7: equivalent|n. 可与之相比的事物

column1: No-one has found one of their canoes or any rigging, which could reveal how the canoes were sailed.
column2: 没有人找到他们的独木舟或任何相关的装备，而这些东西或许能揭示这些独木舟是如何被使用的。

column1: Nor do the oral histories and traditions of later Polynesians offer any insights, for they turn into myths long before they reach as far back in time as the Lapita.
column2: 后来波利尼西亚人的口述历史和传统也毫无启示，因为它们在追溯到拉皮塔时代之前便已演变为神话。

column1: ‘All we can say for certain is that the Lapita had canoes that were capable of ocean voyages, and they had the ability to sail them,’ says Geoff Irwin, a professor of archaeology at the University of Auckland.
column2: ‘我们所能确定的只是，拉皮塔人拥有能够进行海洋航行的独木舟，而且他们具备驾驶这些独木舟的能力，’奥克兰大学考古学教授杰弗·欧文说道。

column1: Those sailing skills, he says, were developed and passed down over thousands of years by earlier mariners who worked their way through the archipelagoes of the western Pacific, making short crossings to nearby islands.
column2: 他说，这些航海技能是更早的航海者历经数千年发展并传承下来的。他们在西太平洋的各个群岛间逐步前行，每次短途航行到附近的岛屿。
column6: over thousands of years|历经数千年
column8: worked their way through|逐步穿行于

column1: The real adventure didn’t begin, however, until their Lapita descendants sailed out of sight of land, with empty horizons on every side.
column2: 然而，真正的冒险才刚刚开始——当他们的拉皮塔后代驶离陆地、四周都是空旷的海洋时。

column1: This must have been as difficult for them as landing on the moon is for us today.
column2: 对他们来说，这一定就像今天我们登陆月球一样困难。

column1: Certainly it distinguished them from their ancestors, but what gave them the courage to launch out on such risky voyages?
column2: 当然，这种差异让他们与祖先们有所不同。但是，究竟是什么让他们有勇气去进行如此危险的航行呢？

column1: The Lapita’s thrust into the Pacific was eastward, against the prevailing trade winds, Irwin notes.
column2: 伊尔文指出，拉皮塔人向太平洋的东进方向，与盛行的信风方向相反。

column1: Those nagging headwinds, he argues, may have been the key to their success.
column2: 他认为，那些令人困扰的逆风，可能是他们成功的关键。

column1: ‘They could sail out for days into the unknown and assess the area, secure in the knowledge that if they didn’t find anything, they could turn about and catch a swift ride back on the trade winds.
column2: “他们可以驶向未知海域，连续航行数天，探察那一带。他们心里有底：即使一无所获，也可以掉头，借着信风迅速返航。
column4: into the unknown|进入未知水域
column6: secure in the knowledge|因知道……而心里有底

column1: This is what would have made the whole thing work.’
column2: 正是这一点使得整个计划能够成功实施。

column1: Once out there, skilled seafarers would have detected abundant leads to follow to land: seabirds, coconuts and twigs carried out to sea by the tides, and the afternoon pile-up of clouds on the horizon which often indicates an island in the distance.
column2: 到了海上，有经验的航海者想必会发现许多能引导他们找到陆地的线索：海鸟，被潮水带到海上的椰子和小树枝，以及午后堆聚在地平线上的云团——云团往往预示着远处有岛。
column3: skilled seafarers|n. 熟练的航海者
column11: pile-up of clouds|n. 云团的积聚

column1: For returning explorers successful or not, the geography of their own archipelagoes would have provided a safety net.
column2: 无论这些回归的探险者是否能够取得成功，他们自己所拥有的群岛地理环境无疑为他们提供了一种安全保障。

column1: Without this to go by, overshooting their home ports, getting lost and sailing off into eternity would have been all too easy.
column2: 如果没有这个参照，船只很容易偏离家乡港口，迷失方向，最终驶向永恒的远方。

column1: Vanuatu, for example, stretches more than 500 miles in a northwest-southeast trend, its scores of intervisible islands forming a backstop for mariners riding the trade winds home.
column2: 以瓦努阿图为例，群岛沿西北至东南方向绵延五百多英里。几十座彼此可以望见的岛屿，给乘信风返乡的航海者提供了最后一道保障。

column1: All this presupposes one essential detail, says Atholl Anderson, professor of prehistory at the Australian National University: the Lapita had mastered the advanced art of sailing against the wind.
column2: 澳大利亚国立大学史前学教授阿索尔·安德森指出，这一切都基于一个关键前提：拉皮塔人已经掌握了逆风航行的高级技巧。

column1: ‘And there’s no proof they could do any such thing,’ Anderson says.
column2: “而且没有证据表明他们真的做了那样的事情，”安德森说道。
column4: do any such thing|做这样的事

column1: ‘There has been this assumption they did, and people have built canoes to re-create those early voyages based on that assumption.
column2: 人们基于这种假设来制作独木舟，以重现那些早期的航行过程。

column1: But nobody has any idea what their canoes looked like or how they were rigged.’
column2: 但是，没有人知道他们的独木舟到底是什么样子的，也不清楚它们是如何组装的。

column1: Rather than give all the credit to human skill, Anderson invokes the winds of chance.
column2: 安德森并没有将所有功劳归于人类技艺，而是强调偶然因素的作用。

column1: El Niño, the same climate disruption that affects the Pacific today, may have helped scatter the Lapita, Anderson suggests.
column2: 安德森认为，如今仍影响太平洋的厄尔尼诺气候异常现象，当年可能也促使拉皮塔人分散到了各地。
column3: El Niño|n. 厄尔尼诺现象

column1: He points out that climate data obtained from slow-growing corals around the Pacific indicate a series of unusually frequent El Niños around the time of the Lapita expansion.
column2: 他指出，从太平洋各地生长缓慢的珊瑚中获取的气候数据显示，在拉皮塔人扩张前后，厄尔尼诺现象接连发生，频率异乎寻常。
column10: unusually frequent|发生得异常频繁的

column1: By reversing the regular east-to-west flow of the trade winds for weeks at a time, these ‘super El Niños’ might have taken the Lapita on long unplanned voyages.
column2: 这些“超级厄尔尼诺”现象每次都使通常自东向西吹的信风反向持续数周，可能就这样把拉皮塔人带上了原本未曾计划的长途航程。
column7: for weeks at a time|每次持续数周
column9: unplanned voyages|n. 原先没有计划的航程

column1: However they did it, the Lapita spread themselves a third of the way across the Pacific, then called it quits for reasons known only to them.
column2: 无论他们如何实现，拉皮塔人将足迹扩展到太平洋三分之一处，然后停止，原因只有他们自己知道。

column1: Ahead lay the vast emptiness of the central Pacific and perhaps they were too thinly stretched to venture farther.
column2: 前方是太平洋中央的广阔荒凉地带，或许他们的队伍过于稀疏，无法继续前进。

column1: They probably never numbered more than a few thousand in total, and in their rapid migration eastward they encountered hundreds of islands - more than 300 in Fiji alone.
column2: 他们的总人数很可能从未超过几千人，却在迅速东迁途中遇到数百座岛屿，单是斐济就有三百多座。
